Running npm run format broke python3 ai/skills/verify-openapi-contract/scripts/check_openapi_contract.py: it re-wrapped 4 controllers' @ApiResponse({...}) decorators (which had previously been manually collapsed to single-line in an earlier cycle) back onto multiple lines because their description text exceeds printWidth 100. The script's boundary heuristic (finding the previous method's closing brace via regex on '\n  }'/'\n}') mistakes a multi-line decorator's own closing '})' line for that boundary, silently truncating the captured decorator block and losing every status code before it — confirmed empirically by isolating the heuristic function and running it against the reformatted file (captured block was empty).

Root-caused that ONLY the last-in-stack multi-line decorator before a handler matters (everything before its close is dropped from capture, everything after survives), so a multi-line @ApiOperation positioned before all @ApiResponse decorators is safe, but every @ApiResponse decorator carrying a required status code must itself render on exactly one line. Computed exact character budgets: with HttpStatus.<NAME> + type + description all inline, every real case in this codebase exceeds 100 chars (up to 313 for the longest), so description text cannot survive inline under the current printWidth. Tested and ruled out '// prettier-ignore' above a decorator in a stack — Prettier does not honor it for an individual decorator among several on the same class member (reproduced with the exact repo prettier config).

Fix: kept status/type inline (required for the script's regex match) on one line in all 4 controllers, moved each description string verbatim into a plain // comment directly above its decorator (no information lost, not shown in generated Swagger UI). Reran npm run format:check (pass, 0 issues) and check_openapi_contract.py (pass, 4 operations) together — both mandatory gates now agree.
